2027-07-11.title: Eighth Sunday after Pentecost
readings: Let anyone with ears to hear listen
Oh, that I knew where I might find him
Obey my voice, and I will be your God
My servants shall sing for gladness of heart
A chosen race, a royal priesthood
The word of God is living and active
Those who hear the word and accept it bear fruit
2027-07-11.alt: Season of Pentecost. (The 2025–26 lectionary lists Mark 4 for both Gospels; check the 2026–27 lectionary.)
2027-07-11.verse: Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
theo: “Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword… able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.” God's word is not a dead letter; it cuts, heals, judges and gives life. When the Gospel is proclaimed in the Qurbono, Christ himself speaks. The question is not whether the word is powerful, but whether we listen.

In Mark's Gospel Jesus begins his teaching by the sea with one word: “Listen!” Then the sower goes out to sow. The seed is the word; the soil is the human heart. “And these are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.” And he ends: “Let anyone with ears to hear listen!” Listening is the first act of faith.

At the burning bush God speaks to Moses and reveals his name: “I AM WHO I AM… This is my name forever.” God is not an idea; he is the living One who speaks and sends: “I will be with you.” Jeremiah repeats God's one demand: “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people.” To obey (in Latin ob-audire) is to listen deeply.

The Letter to the Hebrews joins the Word with mercy: “We do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathise with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy.” St Peter tells us who we have become by listening and believing: “a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people.”
conn: Exodus 3:14: the divine name; Jesus speaks with the same authority: “Listen!”
Jeremiah 7:23: the covenant is listening; Mark 4:20: the good soil hears and accepts.
Job 23:3: Job longs to find God; Hebrews 4:16: in Christ we may approach the throne with boldness.
1 Peter 2:9: the people formed by the Word to declare God's wonders.
altar: In the Holy Qurbono the Word is first proclaimed, then made flesh on the altar. The same Christ who speaks in the Gospel gives himself in the Mysteries; the hearing of the Word prepares the heart to receive the Bread.
outline: “Listen!”: the first word of the parable.
The Word cuts, heals and judges.
The God who speaks and sends.
A high priest who understands our weakness.
“Let anyone with ears to hear listen!”
live: Read the Sunday Gospel again each day this week, slowly, for ten minutes.
Give one person your full attention this week, without interrupting.
Bring a weakness you are ashamed of to Christ in confession.
fathers: Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ (Commentary on Isaiah, Prologue).

Who can grasp all the richness of even one of your words, Lord? What we understand is much less than what we leave behind, like the thirsty who drink from a fountain (Commentary on the Diatessaron 1, 18).
magis: The Church strongly exhorts all the faithful to learn the surpassing knowledge of Jesus Christ by frequent reading of the divine Scriptures.
In the sacred books the Father who is in heaven meets his children with great love and speaks with them.
The whole community of believers is, as such, priestly (1 Peter 2:9).
saints: 11 July: St Benedict. 15 July (Thu): Commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios (1953): Holy Qurbono for the people. 16 July: Our Lady of Mount Carmel.
2027-07-11.prayer: Lord God, I AM WHO I AM, your word is living and active. Open our ears to listen, our hearts to accept, and our lives to bear fruit thirty, sixty and a hundredfold. Through Jesus, our merciful high priest, let us approach your throne of grace with boldness. Amen.

quick: “The word of God is living and active”: Christ speaks when the Gospel is proclaimed.
Good soil hears the word, accepts it, and bears fruit a hundredfold.
Jesus is a high priest who understands our weakness: approach with boldness.
2027-07-11.action: Read the Sunday Gospel again for ten minutes each day this week.
2027-07-11.question: Do I really listen when God's word is read?
2027-07-11.special: Eighth Sunday after Pentecost. Thursday 15 July: Commemoration of Archbishop Mar Ivanios, Holy Qurbono for the people.
illus: In many Kerala homes the Bible is placed on a stand with a lamp beside it, honoured like a guest. Honouring the Book is good; opening it every day is better. The word works only in the heart that listens.

family.explain: God's word is alive! When we read the Bible, God speaks to our hearts like a friend.
family.intention: We pray to listen to God's word every day.
family.ask: Ask: “What did God say to us in today's Gospel?”

catechism: Scripture in the life of the Church.
The common priesthood of the faithful.
kidsaint: A young man who left the noisy city to pray in a cave, and later founded monasteries where monks prayed and worked. His Rule begins with the word “Listen.” Lesson: to hear God, we need quiet hearts.
term: In the Syro-Malankara Qurbono the Gospel (Evangelion) is proclaimed by the priest with candles and incense, and the people stand, because Christ himself speaks.
termMore: All the baptised share in Christ's priesthood (1 Peter 2:9): they offer their lives, prayers and work as spiritual sacrifices. This common priesthood differs in essence, not only in degree, from the ministerial priesthood of bishops and priests (Lumen Gentium 10).

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Letter to the Hebrews says: “The word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword.” When the Gospel is read in the Holy Qurbono, it is not a story from long ago. Christ himself speaks to us now. That is why we stand, why the candles and the incense honour the Book.

In Mark's Gospel Jesus begins his parable with one word: “Listen!” and ends with another: “Let anyone with ears to hear listen!” In between is the sower. The same seed falls on the path, on rock, among thorns, and on good soil. Good soil is the heart that hears the word, accepts it, and lets it bear fruit, thirty, sixty, a hundredfold.

At the burning bush God told Moses his name: “I AM WHO I AM.” The living God speaks. Jeremiah says that God asked only one thing of Israel: “Obey my voice.” To obey means to listen deeply. Much of our trouble comes from not listening: to God, to one another.

And if we are afraid that the Word will judge us, Hebrews adds: we have a high priest who understands our weakness, who was tested in every way as we are, yet without sin. “Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy.” This week give ten minutes each day to the Gospel. Listen. And let the word bear fruit. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once began a story with one word: “Listen!” Can you say it? Listen!
A farmer threw seeds. Some fell on the path, some on rocks, some in thorns, and some in good soil. The good soil gave lots and lots of fruit!
God's word is the seed, and your heart is the soil. Let's listen to Jesus every day and be good soil!

intro: Theme: “Let anyone with ears to hear listen.”
Jesus tells the parable of the sower. The Letter to the Hebrews calls God's word living and active. The God who revealed his name to Moses speaks to us, and calls us his own priestly people.

sub: God's word never returns empty; the problem is never the seed.
The path, the rocky ground and the thorns are hearts closed by hardness, shallowness or worry.
Good soil hears, accepts and bears fruit with patience.
q: So shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
And these are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.
points.apply: Ask yourself honestly which soil your heart is this week, and remove one “thorn”.

points.h: The word is living and active
sub: God asks above all: “Obey my voice.”
His word judges the thoughts of the heart; it is a sword that heals.
In the Holy Qurbono, when the Gospel is proclaimed, Christ himself speaks (Second Vatican Council, Sacrosanctum Concilium 7).
q: But this command I gave them, “Obey my voice, and I will be your God, and you shall be my people; and walk only in the way that I command you, so that it may be well with you.”

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel again at home and keep one verse in your heart.

points.h: A people who belong to “I AM”
sub: God revealed his name to Moses: “I AM WHO I AM.”
Through baptism we become a chosen race, a royal priesthood.
This common priesthood of the faithful is lived by offering our lives with Christ, and is served by the ministerial priesthood.
q: God said to Moses, “I AM WHO I AM.” He said further, “Thus you shall say to the Israelites, ‘I AM has sent me to you.’”
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
points.apply: Offer your daily work to God each morning as your spiritual sacrifice.

concl: The Sower is generous; the word is powerful; the harvest depends on our listening.
Let us be good soil and a priestly people.
2027-07-11.resolve: Give ten minutes each day this week to reading the Gospel of Mark.
